title: ‘सोतला’ उपन्यासको विश्लेषण
authors: राई Rai, राम कुमार Ram Kumar
nepali: डोरबहादुरद्वारा लिखित ‘सोतला’ उपन्यास तिब्बत चिनको स्वशासित क्षेत्रमा परिणत हुनुभन्दा अगाडि नै नेपाल र तिब्बतको बिचमा घनिष्ट सम्बन्ध स्थापित भइसकेको थियो भन्ने साहित्यिक दस्तावेज हो । सोतला उपन्यासलाई प्राथमिक सामग्री मानेर गुणात्मक ढाँचामा विवेच्य उपन्यासको अध्ययन विश्लेषणलाई मूल विधि मानेर प्रस्तुत लेख तयार गरिएको छ । यसमा नेपाल परापूर्व कालदेखि नै त्यस भूमिसँग नेपालीहरुको गहिरो सम्बन्ध रहिआएको अभिव्यक्तिहरु पाइन्छन्। त्यस्तै नेपाल र तिब्बत बिचको सामाजिक–सांस्कृतिक सम्बन्ध, ऐतिहासिक राजनैतिक परिवेश, गरिबीसँगको सङ्घर्षको क्रममा उपत्यकाली युवकहरु ल्हासा पुग्नु, त्यसपछि धर्म, संस्कृति र भेष–भूषा–भाषामा समेत समिश्रण आउनु, नेपाल र तिब्बत बिचको व्यापारिक सम्बन्ध र त्यसको स्थिति, त्यस क्रममा दुई सांस्कृतिक व्यक्तिहरुका वा तिब्बती र उपत्यकाली नेवारहरु बिचको वैवाहिक सम्बन्ध र सन्तानको जन्म, सांस्कृतिक विषमता एवम् सामाजिक अन्ध विश्वासका कारण खच्चड संस्कृतिको जन्म, नेपाली सरकारी कर्मचारीको भ्रष्टचारी घुसखोरी प्रवृत्ति, व्यापारिक बेइमानी र नाफाखोरी प्रवृत्तिका कारण साना व्यापारीहरुले भोग्नु परेका समस्याहरुलाई उपन्यासले प्रस्तुत गरेको छ र यस लेखमा उपन्यासका ती पाटाहरुको विश्लेषण गर्ने कार्य गरिएको छ ।
american_english: The novel 'Sotala', written by Dor Bahadur, is a literary document showing that a close relationship between Nepal and Tibet had already been established before Tibet became China's autonomous region. Treating the novel Sotala as primary material, this article has been prepared in a qualitative format, taking the study and analysis of the novel under discussion as the main method. In it, expressions are found showing that Nepal has had a deep relationship with that land since ancient times. Similarly, the social-cultural relationship between Nepal and Tibet, the historical political context, the reaching of valley youths to Lhasa in the course of the struggle with poverty, the subsequent blending even in religion, culture and dress, adornment and language, the trade relationship between Nepal and Tibet and its condition, in that course the marital relationship between two culturally distinct persons or between Tibetans and valley Newars and the birth of children, the birth of a mixed culture due to cultural disparity and social blind belief, the corrupt bribe-taking tendency of Nepali government employees, the problems small traders had to face because of the tendencies of commercial dishonesty and profiteering — these have been presented by the novel, and in this article the work of analyzing those aspects of the novel has been done.

informal_english: The novel 'Sotala' by Dor Bahadur is basically a literary document showing that Nepal and Tibet were already close as anything before Tibet became China's autonomous region. This article was put together in a qualitative way, treating the novel as primary material and taking the study and analysis of the novel in question as the main method. In it you find expressions showing that Nepal has had a deep bond with that land since ancient times. Similarly, the social and cultural relationship between Nepal and Tibet, the historical political context, valley youths making their way to Lhasa while struggling with poverty, the blending that then crept into religion, culture, dress, adornment and language, the trade relationship between Nepal and Tibet and how it stood, the marital relationships between culturally distinct people — Tibetans and valley Newars — and the children born of them, the birth of a mixed culture born of cultural disparity and social blind belief, the corrupt bribe-taking ways of Nepali government employees, the problems small traders had to put up with because of commercial dishonesty and profiteering — all of these are presented by the novel, and this article does the work of analysing those aspects of it.
translator_notes: Sentence order preserved; the final sentence is a single long enumeration in the source and is kept as one sentence. 'Khachchar' (mule) culture rendered as 'mixed culture'.
